title: ZNF512B associates with mitotic spindles; regulates metaphase exit; and is crucial for stem cell differentiation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed 2 of the 8 processed files in GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE303898: GSE303898_DESeq2_CM_KO4_WT.csv.gz and GSE303898_DESeq2_naive_WT_KO4.csv.gz. Each is semicolon-separated with 25,209 rows and 7 columns (gene name; base mean; log2 (FC) = log2 fold change; stad err; wald-stats; p-value; adj p-value). Listed the whole GEO supplementary directory (8 files, 621-664 KB gzipped, all DESeq2 contrast tables, no per-sample count matrix). Read GEO series metadata: 27 samples, mouse (Mus musculus), naive/primed/cardiomyocyte/neural-progenitor states in wild type and two Zfp512b knockout clones. Fetched the PRIDE (proteomics repository) record for PXD078292: licence CC0, submission type PARTIAL, timsTOF HT instrument, MaxQuant processing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That significant differentially expressed genes were called at adjusted p-value < 0.05 and listed in Supplementary Tables S1/S2, and that >3000 genes change in naive knockout cells. The paper's supplementary files were not retrievable (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles returned HTTP 500). The PRIDE per-file listing timed out twice, so I could not confirm whether any processed protein-intensity table accompanies the raw mass-spectrometry files; a PARTIAL submission usually means raw files plus search output only.

a1_downloadable.note: All 8 GEO processed tables download without login; PRIDE dataset is public and CC0. Verified by downloading two GEO files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: log2 fold change and adjusted p-value are literal columns in the downloaded CSVs, so a differential-expression label needs no construction.

a3_inputs_present.note: The files contain only a gene symbol per row - no sequence, no promoter, no feature of any kind. Every input would have to be imported wholesale from Ensembl or another resource; the dataset supplies labels only.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns are self-describing (base mean, log2 fold change, standard error, Wald statistic, p-value, adjusted p-value); DESeq2 v1.46.0 named in methods.

a5_enough_rows.note: 25,209 gene rows per contrast, but only 8 contrasts from 27 samples of one cell line and one knocked-out gene with two clones - the independent unit is the experiment, not the gene, so there is effectively one labelled perturbation.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~5 MB uncompressed across all 8 DESeq2 tables
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; raw sequencing stays in SRA (BioProject PRJNA1298190) and would not be touched.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper's '>3000 deregulated genes in naive knockout' is consistent with the file; exact supplementary table counts unverifiable because the supplement returned HTTP 500.

a8_label_provenance.note: log2 fold change derives from featureCounts read counts and DESeq2 on real RNA-seq, not from another model's prediction; it is not computable from any feature in the file.

existing_models.name: DeepLoc (deep neural network predicting protein subcellular localization from sequence alone)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported high accuracy on curated UniProt localization classes; I retrieved the paper record only and did not verify a number or split for a spindle-specific class.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Fine-grained compartments such as the mitotic spindle are not among the classes these tools resolve; the retrieved review of localization predictors notes no spindle-specific predictor.

existing_models.name: PromoterAI (deep network scoring promoter variants for expression change)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published 2025 in Science on human promoter variants; retrieved as evidence that sequence-to-expression-change modelling is an active, well-served area, not as a baseline for this knockout.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer of sequence-to-expression models to new cell types and perturbations remains weak - named in the retrieved Nature Reviews Genetics 2025 review of sequence-to-expression models.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA language model)
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice for the data volume, but there is no task with enough labels to fit a head
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT; GEO data public domain; PRIDE dataset CC0

integration.partner_dataset: Human Protein Atlas subcellular localization and mouse Ensembl/BioMart promoter annotation
integration.join_key: gene symbol to Ensembl gene ID (mouse)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No combined question survives: joining a single-gene knockout's fold changes to a localization atlas would add partners but still leave one perturbation and one cell line, which cannot support a generalizable prediction.

controls.positive_control: Zfp512b itself should be the most strongly reduced gene in the knockout contrasts - a sanity check on the files, not a model control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable on the gene table, but with one perturbation there is nothing meaningful to shuffle against.
controls.external_validation: None: no second independent Zfp512b knockout expression dataset was found, and the two clones come from the same lab and selection.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built here could only claim 'predicts which mouse genes shift when Zfp512b is deleted, in two clones of one embryonic stem cell line from one lab' - a statement about one experiment, not a transferable rule.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use promoter DNA sequence to predict which genes change when the Zfp512b gene is deleted in mouse stem cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene-level results from 8 comparisons of wild type versus two Zfp512b knockout clones across four stem cell states; 25,209 gene rows per comparison, verified in the downloaded files, but inputs would have to be fetched from Ensembl because the files hold only gene symbols.
plain_idea.predict: The log2 fold change, or an up/down/unchanged call, measured by RNA sequencing of 27 samples and processed with featureCounts and DESeq2 in one lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chromatin researchers would like to know which promoter features make a gene responsive to loss of a repressor; even a failed model would quantify how little of a single knockout's response is written in promoter sequence.

more_or_better_data.why: Sequence-to-expression models such as Enformer and PromoterAI train on thousands of human and mouse samples; this contributes 27 samples from one cell line and one gene.

confidence_score.why: Only two knockout clones and 2-3 replicates per state; that supports a crude noise estimate but not per-gene calibrated confidence.

models_beatable.why: The relevant models (PromoterAI 2025, Enformer 2021 onward) are recent, large and honestly evaluated, and this data offers no slice they cover badly.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The existing models cannot be run as a baseline on this label (they predict expression, not knockout response), the inputs are absent from the files, and no matching split exists.

label_elsewhere.sources: Searched for a second Zfp512b/ZNF512B knockout expression dataset and for any spindle-association predictor; found neither. The paper's own bioRxiv preprint is the same data.
label_elsewhere.why: The label - response to loss of this one protein - exists only in this study, so there is no external training data and no independent validation set.

ml_idea: Considered predicting Zfp512b-knockout responsiveness (log2 fold change, or up/down/unchanged) for 25,209 mouse genes from promoter sequence embeddings plus baseline expression, with the two knockout clones used as a replication check. Rejected: the files supply labels but no inputs, and all 201,672 label rows trace to a single perturbation in a single cell line.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the files I actually downloaded: 8 gzipped CSVs totalling ~5 MB, 25,209 rows each, parsed in seconds with pandas; the 6 hours is for symbol-to-Ensembl mapping and promoter extraction, which I did not do.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent perturbations: one gene, one cell line, two clones, 27 samples. That count kills it before any file is opened.

verdict_reason: Fails A3 and A5. The 8 downloaded DESeq2 tables hold 25,209 gene rows each with a clean log2 fold change column, but they contain no model inputs at all - only gene symbols - and every row describes the same single experiment: deletion of one gene in one mouse embryonic stem cell line, two clones, 27 RNA-seq samples. The gene count masquerades as sample size, as with the scCT-DB candidate. The mass-spectrometry dataset (PXD078292) is a PARTIAL submission of pull-down raw files whose per-file listing was unreachable, and would in any case describe a handful of pull-downs. This is a well-executed single-gene cell biology paper with no ML-sized question inside it.
